title: prompt-contract.v1 — frozen render+parse contract objects (eval/prompt_contract.py). The contract exists so every track serves BYTE-IDENTICAL prompts and applies IDENTICAL reply-acceptance rules; contract_sha is the version pin that makes cross-run numbers comparable.

sha16.description: First 16 hex chars of a sha256 — long enough to be collision-safe at corpus scale, short enough to eyeball-diff in logs.

manifest.description: Output of contract_manifest(): the self-description a run embeds so a reader can verify WHICH template/parser produced its prompts without re-reading code.

profile.description: adding a profile mints a new contract_sha

contract_sha.description: stable id of the (template, plan policy, user policy, parser) tuple; depends on module constants ONLY — never on rows, env, clock, or the Java working tree

parser_spec.description: bumping the parser bumps contract_sha — acceptance-rule changes are version changes, not silent drift

system_template_sha.description: sha256 of the seven frozen SYS_*_V1 literals concatenated in assembly order, recomputed from the literals at call time; equals frozen_against_java_sha iff nobody tampered with the pasted literals

plan_policy.description: plans come from eval/decks/<slug>.plan; plan CONTENT is pinned per-render by plan_sha, deliberately OUTSIDE contract_sha so a .plan edit is detectable without moving the contract version

user_policy.description: the user message is the logged prompt byte-for-byte — no reflow, no normalization — so the model sees exactly what the original seat saw

frozen_against_java_sha.description: sha of the PreambleBuilder pieces AS OBSERVED AT FREEZE TIME. If the working-tree Java drifts later, v1 stays frozen on purpose; mint v2 to adopt.

static_reference_included.description: live games today (BUILDS['FIX']) do not send STATIC_REFERENCE on the smart tier, so the contract does not either — appending it would serve a preamble no logged game ever saw

rendered.description: Output of render(): the exact two-message prompt plus the parse geometry (menu numbers, decline slot, PASS index) the parser will enforce. render_sha pins the served bytes per item.

decision_type.description: harness decision type (play/target/mulligan/...); drives family and choice encoding

family.description: replay_match.decision_family(decision_type). 'unknown' renders (the prompt is verbatim anyway) but parse() returns unsupported_family — never a guessed acceptance rule

menu_numbers.description: the 1-based numbers the parser will accept as an OPTION. For type=='play' the LAST of these IS the PASS option; mulligan is [1,2] (KEEP=1, MULLIGAN=2 — wire format is the words, numbers exist only for lenient bare-number recovery)

decline_menu_number.description: non-play single types only: decideOne's extra decline slot at n_options+1, which has NO entry in options and logs choice=-1. null elsewhere (play declines VIA its PASS option)

pass_option_index.description: n_options-1 for type=='play' (the trailing 'PASS (do nothing)' option), null otherwise

plan_slug.description: archetype slug the plan resolved to (eval/decks/*.plan stem), null when unresolved/unknown

plan_sha.description: sha256(plan_text)[:16] — pins the plan CONTENT per render, the deliberate counterpart to contract_sha pinning the template (a .plan edit moves this, not the contract version)

plan_source.description: how the plan text was obtained; 'unresolved' serves an empty plan block, exactly like the harness does for a seat with no plan

messages.description: messages[0] = frozen system template assembled with (seat, plan); messages[1] = row.prompt VERBATIM including the numbered menu and format tail

render_sha.description: sha256(system + '\x00' + user)[:16] — byte-level proof two runs served the same prompt

warnings.description: additive row-hygiene notes; n_options (the harness's count) is trusted over len(options) and the discrepancy is recorded rather than silently patched

parsed.description: Output of parse(). THE core semantic: outcome=='interface_failure' means the reply could not become a legal action and is NEVER scored as a wrong Magic play — a model bad at output format must be distinguishable from a model bad at Magic.

interface_error.description: null when ok. empty_reply: reply None/blank. no_tag: no CHOICE/ANSWER/PICKS/BLOCKS/KEEP|MULLIGAN anywhere. no_number: tag present but no digit run after it (observed: replies truncated to 'CHOICE: '). out_of_range: number parsed but not a menu number nor the decline slot — an interface failure in BOTH strictnesses; the live harness's silent out-of-range->PASS coercion is deliberately refused. count_out_of_range: blocks family emitted more assignments than legal blockers. unsupported_family: v1 has no acceptance rule for this decision type.

recovered_by.description: lenient only: no tag found but the last non-empty line held exactly one digit run that was in range. Leniency is about FORMAT, never LEGALITY.

menu_number.description: raw 1-based number the model emitted (recorded even when out of range, so the formatting tax is auditable)

option_index.description: 0-based index into options; None when the model picked the decline slot (which has no options entry). For play PASS this IS n_options-1 (PASS is a real option) even though choice is -1.

choice.description: harness log encoding (EVAL contract §1.3) so equality against logged rows is direct: single/mulligan -> option index or -1 for PASS/decline; count -> picks_size; blocks -> blocks_count. null on interface failure.

picks.description: count family: sorted 0-based distinct in-range picks. 'PICKS: NONE' is a VALID size-0 pick (matches the harness), not a failure.

blocks_count.description: blocks family: number of 'X->Y' assignments ('BLOCKS: NONE' -> 0). Pairings are not parseable into indices in v1 (they were never logged).

raw.description: the reply exactly as given (None for transport failure), kept so failures stay auditable

is_pass.description: true only for type=='play' when the model chose the trailing PASS menu number; distinguishes an EXPLICIT pass from the harness's -1 sentinel that historically also swallowed formatting failures
